items.title: Sarawak targets 20,000 affordable homes by 2030, says deputy minister
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 29 — The Sarawak government will continue working with the housing industry to meet the people’s housing needs, including its target of building 20,000 affordable homes by 2030. State Deputy Minister of Public Health, Housing and Local Government Datuk Michael Tiang said collaboration with industry players remained important in ensuring housing was suitable, of good quality and responsive to the needs of Sarawakians. And where improvements are needed, let us find practical solutions together,” he said when officiating at Sarawak Housing Real Estate Developers Association (Sheda) Home and Property Roadshow 2026 at Wisma Sanyan here yesterday.

items.title: Called a ‘gambling boss’, Anwar fires back: I cut special lottery draws from 22 to eight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hit back at critics branding him a “ tauke judi ”, or gambling boss, saying his government had instead cut the number of special lottery draws from 22 a year to eight. Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the reduction showed his administration had taken steps to curb gaming activities. “You held 22 special draws, but I reduced it to eight.

items.title: Kepong MP wants IGP to explain double standards over Jalur Gemilang display errors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A government backbencher today called on Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail to explain allegations of double standards in investigations into cases involving the incorrect display of the Jalur Gemilang. Kepong member of Parliament Lim Lip Eng said if the mistake in displaying the Jalur Gemilang was genuinely unintentional, promptly corrected and followed by an apology, no one should be arrested. "The Inspector-General of Police must immediately explain this double standard," he said.

items.title: Ahmad Zahid congratulates Wakaf Tapai IKBN student on international championship win
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has congratulated Wakaf Tapai National Youth Skills Institute (IKBN) student Muhammad Ammar Azli on winning the welding category at the Finals of the Professional Skills Championship (Professionals 2026) in Kaluga, Russia. The Rural and Regional Development Minister said the achievement once again demonstrated that the country's technical and vocational education and training (TVET) students have the talent and skills to compete with the world's best on the international stage. "Congratulations, Muhammad Ammar!

items.title: Retired soldiers turn homes into 'Galeri Merdeka' with 300 Jalur Gemilang flags
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Their days in military service may be over, but Yusof Abu Talib and Abd Razak Mohd Jai continue to show their patriotism and love for the country by turning their homes into what they describe as "Galeri Merdeka". In conjunction with this year's 69th National Day celebrations, the two in-laws, who live in neighbouring houses, have adorned their homes in Kampung Lendu, here, with more than 300 Jalur Gemilang flags and various Independence-themed decorations. [[nid:1521154]] Yusof, 54, said the idea stemmed from their desire to continue fostering love for the country even though they were no longer serving in the military.

items.title: Merdeka Day parade to proceed if clear skies remain
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Merdeka Day parade on Monday will proceed as scheduled if clear skies remain, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said a meeting was held yesterday afternoon involving the Meteorological Department, Environment Department, Health Ministry and Education Ministry. "We have decided that if conditions remain as they are this morning (clear skies) and yesterday, we will proceed with the event on Monday," he said after the National Day 2026 parade rehearsal in Putrajaya today.

items.title: CIMB doubles down on dividend payout of above 55pct despite Indonesia headwinds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd is doubling down on its dividend payout ratio of above 55 per cent despite challenges in Indonesia, group chief executive officer Novan Amirudin said. We are a diversified business," he said. Group chief financial officer Khairul Rifaie said the bank's net interest income (NII) growth was underpinned by strong total asset growth, supported by a healthy pipeline that would continue to drive NII growth.

items.title: Trump announces new US 'Space Academy'
items.summary: Trump announces new US 'Space Academy' AFP JOHNSON SPACE CENTRE: President Donald Trump on Friday announced the creation of a "Space Academy" to train future civilian and military recruits for an arena where the United States faces rivalry with China. Speaking at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, Trump said the institution would be modeled on the famed US military academy at West Point. "It's called the U.S. Space Academy.

items.title: Police arrest two men for allegedly impersonating enforcement officers to extort RM1,500 from foreigner in Penampang
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Aug 29 — Police have arrested two local men for allegedly posing as enforcement officers and attempting to extort RM1,500 from a foreign national at Kampung Koidupan Sugud here early yesterday. Penampang district police chief Supt Sammy Newton said the incident occurred at about 12.10am when the suspects, aged 19 and 28, allegedly approached the victim wearing attire resembling enforcement agency uniforms and demanded to see his identification documents. Police also seized several pieces of clothing resembling enforcement agency uniforms, which are believed to have been worn by the suspects during the incident.

items.title: Perak to consider RM500 first-marriage incentive under 2027 state budget
items.summary: Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said the motion proposing the special incentive was unanimously approved during the recent fifth sitting of the Perak Youth Assembly. Khairudin said the proposed assistance would target youths aged between 15 and 35, in line with the definition of youth under the Youth Development and Sports Act 2007. Meanwhile, Khairudin said the National Youth Premier Award featured three categories, namely male individual, female individual and youth organisation, while the State Youth Special Award comprised seven categories, all fully funded by the state government.

items.title: Water disruption expected as Sarawak Water conducts Jalan Matang pipeline repairs Sept 4-5; traffic diversion from Sept 3-12
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 29 — Sarawak Water Sdn Bhd (Sarawak Water) will carry out planned repair works on a 1,100mm-diameter water pipeline along Jalan Matang here from 10pm on September 4 to noon on September 5. The pipeline is one of Sarawak Water’s main pipelines supplying treated water to the Bukit Siol Reservoir, which serves consumers in Kuching, Petra Jaya and surrounding areas. During the repair, consumers in affected areas may experience low water pressure or temporary disruption to their water supply.

items.title: Govt monitoring inflation to avoid cost pressure on the people amid West Asia crisis, says deputy minister
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 29 — The government is monitoring inflation movements due to developments in the West Asian crisis to ensure cost pressures from supply disruptions and rising commodity prices do not burden the people. Deputy Economy Minister Datuk Seri Mohd Shahar Abdullah said the monitoring is important because developments in West Asia are changing rapidly and can potentially impact global supply chains and commodity prices. He said the government is also ensuring the country’s supply, especially for strategic commodities such as oil, remains sufficient until the end of the year while taking appropriate measures to mitigate the crisis’s impact on the domestic economy.

items.title: Penang factory fire leaves owner with first-degree burns
items.summary: Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 6.09pm. He said firefighters took almost 10 hours to completely extinguish the fire. "The fire was completely extinguished at 4.35am today," he said.

items.title: Perak mulls RM500 first‑time marriage incentive to ease financial burden on youths ahead of 2027 state budget
items.summary: Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said the motion proposing the special incentive was unanimously approved during the recent fifth sitting of the Perak Youth Assembly. Khairudin said the proposed assistance would target youths aged between 15 and 35, in line with the definition of youth under the Youth Development and Sports Act 2007 (Act 668). Meanwhile, Khairudin said the National Premier Youth Award featured three categories, namely male individual, female individual and youth organisation, while the State Special Youth Award comprised seven categories fully funded by the state government.

items.title: Sabah clam hunter survives crocodile attack after friend beats nine-foot reptile on the head
items.summary: Hamdan Samad suffered injuries to his left leg and right hand in the 4pm incident. Kampung Weston Village Chief Masri Latif, when contacted by the Daily Express yesterday, said the victim was taken to hospital for treatment. “The crocodile suddenly attacked him and he struggled with the reptile,” Masri said.

items.title: Fire destroys 80 per cent of food stall, storage facility in Ampang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A food stall and a storage facility were almost destroyed in a fire in front of a school near Pekan Ampang, Ampang, here, early this morning. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said a team from the Ampang Fire and Rescue Station was deployed to the scene after the department received an emergency call at 3.46am. He said the fire involved two premises owned by different people, namely a food stall and a general storage facility.

items.title: Kota Belud car wash crash sparks deja vu weeks after Kota Kinabalu International Airport smash
items.summary: KOTA BELUD, Aug 29 — In a scene reminiscent of another that brought down a glass door at the Kota Kinabalu International Airport earlier this month, a 61-year-old driver lost control of her Perodua Ativa and crashed into a Perodua Alza and car wash along Jalan Raya, Thursday. Kota Belud District Police Chief Supt Khairul Shah Peri said the incident occurred at 9.30am after the woman had finished using the automatic car wash. “Initial investigations found that the driver lost control of her vehicle after exiting the automatic car wash machine,” he said in a statement yesterday. The Ativa then veered off and crashed into the Alza parked nearby before hitting the iron structure of the automatic car wash.

items.title: Umno allows state leaders to negotiate cooperation with any party for next election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Umno has agreed to give its state leadership the mandate to hold discussions and negotiations with any political party interested in cooperating in the next election. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the decision was among the resolutions reached at the party’s Supreme Council meeting held last night. The meeting, which began at 8.45pm, was chaired by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and attended by deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and Supreme Council members.

items.title: Patriotism flies high all year at Nor Ashikin's Jalur Gemilang-adorned home
items.summary: JERTIH: Upon stepping into the compound of her home, one's attention is immediately drawn to the fluttering Jalur Gemilang and colourful patriotic decorations adorning almost every corner, creating the impression that National Month is celebrated there all year round. For local food vendor Nor Ashikin Shafiee, 42, decorating her home in Kampung Baru Tok Dor with patriotic-themed ornaments has become a way of life. She said her passion for decorating went beyond simply beautifying her home, describing it as her personal way of nurturing patriotism in her daily life.

items.title: UiTM must remain accessible to underprivileged Bumiputera students, says Sultan Sharafuddin
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 29 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah wants Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) to remain a gateway to social mobility for Malay and Bumiputera youths from low-income families and rural areas. His Royal Highness said that as UiTM grew and progressed, the target group for whom the institution was originally established should not be left behind or distanced from higher education opportunities. “That is the core spirit of UiTM’s struggle that must never be lost,” His Royal Highness said at the UiTM 2026 Royal Address at Dewan Konsert Seri Budiman here today.

items.title: Factory owner suffers first-degree burns trying to fight blaze that destroys 80pc of Butterworth premises
items.summary: Penang Fire and Rescue Department Fire and Rescue Operations Division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 6.09pm. “The fire involved a semi-permanent factory that processes fabric for use in sofas. “The fire was brought under control at 6.28pm, with firefighting efforts also assisted by nearby volunteer fire brigades and an excavator belonging to a private company,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Sabah band Tompuvan wins Asian Folk award at 2026 ICMA
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah-based Borneo ethnic fusion band Tompuvan has won The Best of Asia — Asian Folk award at the 2026 InterContinental Music Awards (ICMA) for their original song, "The Last Warrior". "The Last Warrior" is rooted in Sabah's indigenous heritage and combines traditional Borneo sounds with contemporary music to explore survival, identity, heritage and unity. Tompuvan also shared the award with Malaysian artist Elica Paujin, whose song "Oh Huminodun" was also among the five winners in the category.

items.title: Govt to continue upholding UiTM’s role in Bumiputera development, says Zambry
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 29 — The government will continue to uphold Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) as a key institution in the educational, professional and socioeconomic development of the Bumiputera community. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the mandate and identity that formed the basis for UiTM’s establishment and development would continue to be preserved by the government. “The mandate and identity that formed the basis for UiTM’s establishment and development will continue to be preserved, but defending UiTM does not mean merely preserving what already exists.

items.title: Sarawak wakes to worsening haze as API breaches 200 in three locations
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 29 — Lubok Antu, Sri Aman and Lundu recorded very unhealthy air quality as of 8am on Saturday, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings of 225, 222 and 203 respectively. Nine locations recorded unhealthy air quality, led by Serian at 193 and Sarikei at 188. The remaining six locations recorded moderate air quality — Samalaju at 93, ILP Miri (70), Miri (68), Lawas (67), Bario (64) and Limbang (55).

items.title: Rantau Panjang traders optimistic school holidays will boost sales despite Narathiwat incident
items.summary: PASIR MAS: Concerns among residents in the border area following a security incident in Narathiwat, Thailand, have not deterred traders in Rantau Panjang from hoping for an influx in visitors during the nine-day school holiday that began yesterday. However, a Bernama survey at the Rantau Panjang Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security Complex (ICQS) and around the town found that conditions on the second day of the school holidays remained under control, with traders expecting an increase in visitors over the weekend and ahead of National Day on Aug 31. Food and Thai products trader Afifa Umar, 42, said although visitor numbers were currently not as high as before, the school holidays gave traders hope of increasing their income as more people visit the duty-free area.

items.title: Police detain seven Yemeni men after viral video of dangerous car stunt at Jalan Sungai Besi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Police have detained seven Yemeni nationals to assist in investigations into an incident involving two cars being driven dangerously along Jalan Sungai Besi here early yesterday. Preliminary investigations revealed that the incident occurred at about 12.30 am on Aug 28 while the two vehicles were travelling along Jalan Sungai Besi towards Jalan Bukit Bintang. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station.

items.title: Trump announces deal for huge US stake in Venezuelan oil reserves
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday his administration has reached a huge oil deal with Venezuela that gives the United States majority control of 65 billion barrels of proven petroleum reserves. The deal – which Trump proclaimed as "the biggest oil deal in world history" – will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment to Venezuela, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said. Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves.

items.title: 2027 Budget will ensure country's economic sustainability and resilience, says deputy minister
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The 2027 Budget, which will be tabled in October, will ensure the sustainability of the national economy so that it remains within the projected economic growth range. Deputy Economy Minister Datuk Seri Mohd Shahar Abdullah said although economic growth forecast remained at between four and five per cent, the country's gross domestic product (GDP) growth for the second quarter stood at six per cent. "The second quarter recorded six per cent growth, but we are not taking this as a reason to be complacent.

items.title: Judiciary vital in upholding justice and people’s well‑being, says Tengku Maimun
items.summary: BANGI, Aug 29 — The Judiciary is a vital institution and a key pillar in upholding justice, safeguarding the well-being of the people, and preserving the nation’s integrity, said former Chief Justice Tun Dr Tengku Maimun Tuan Mat. She said the institution plays a crucial role in ensuring transparency and fairness under the Federal Constitution, while safeguarding the rule of law. Tengku Maimun, a Professor of Practice at the UKM Faculty of Law (FUU), also holds the Tuanku Muhriz Royal Chair in Integrity and Good Governance.

items.title: Nine years in remand, murder trial still at prosecution stage: Orang Asli man finally released
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — An Orang Asli man has been freed after spending nine years in remand while his murder trial was still at the prosecution stage, in a case his lawyer said had dragged on for far too long. His lawyer, Kamal Hisham Jaafar, said Jambi had originally been charged with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code and had remained in custody as proceedings continued. “Jambi was originally charged with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code.

items.title: Woman prepared her brother's meals every day, until fire claimed him
items.summary: Azizah never knew that yesterday would be the last time she would do so for her 60-year-old brother, Zakaria. "Every day at about 4pm, I would deliver food to my brother. Azizah said their youngest brother, Harun, 54, would deliver breakfast to Zakaria at about 7.30am every day.

items.title: Prime Minister’s National Day 2026 address set for 2pm at PICC
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — The 2026 National Day Prime Minister’s Address Ceremony at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here has been scheduled for 2 pm, according to the Ministry of National Unity (KPN). “The 2026 National Day Prime Minister’s 2026 Address Ceremony is an important platform to reflect on the aspirations and hopes of the Madani government leadership in fuelling the spirit of independence, strengthening patriotism, and nurturing a sense of love and responsibility towards the country. The National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 Celebration Working Committee under the Ministry of Communications had earlier announced that the Prime Minister’s address ceremony had been moved from Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur to PICC due to the current haze conditions.

items.title: Spain urges calm after anti-migrant protesters clash with police
items.summary: MADRID: Spain's interior minister called for calm on Friday after residents of Ceuta clashed with police during protests against migrants who have remained in the North African enclave following a mass influx. Tensions have been high in the territory of 80,000 inhabitants since tens of thousands of people crossed into Ceuta from Morocco over several days in July, triggering a Europe-wide migrant alert. Two more arrests were made after migrants attacked a police officer, sources said.

items.title: Foreign Ministry says 36 Malaysians in Tibet reported safe, with checks widening to Chinese border areas
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Thirty-six Malaysians in Tibet, China have reported to be safe following flash floods and landslides in the China-Nepal border area. Foreign Ministry deputy secretary-general (Bilateral Relations) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin said that the identities and status of the 36 Malaysians were still being verified with Chinese authorities, and they are cross-checking for any overlap with the list of Malaysians who remained uncontactable in Nepal. The Foreign Ministry’s Operations Room in Putrajaya would continue to operate round the clock to coordinate information, assist Malaysians in the affected areas and provide the latest updates to family members, Syed Mohamad Hasrin said, adding that they would continue seeking confirmation from Chinese authorities regarding the whereabouts and safety of Malaysians in Tibet before drawing any further conclusions.

items.title: Why remand Kulai pair but not Perak MCA staff? Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng asks police after flag gaffe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng today accused the police of applying double standards in their handling of Jalur Gemilang cases, contrasting the four-day remand of two people in Kulai with the questioning, without detention, of those involved in an incident at the Perak MCA headquarters. Does police action depend on who is involved?” Lim said in a statement today.

items.title: Haze: Sri Aman air quality worsens as API reading hits 222 this morning
items.summary: According to the Environment Department's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 29 other areas, mostly in Sarawak, Perak and the Klang Valley, also recorded unhealthy API readings. In Perak, five air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Taiping (155), Tanjung Malim (154), Tasek Ipoh (147), Seri Manjung (119) and Pegoh Ipoh (101). Cheras and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded unhealthy API readings of 160 and 155 respectively, while Putrajaya recorded an unhealthy API reading of 152.

items.title: PAS shuts door on Bersatu reconciliation, excludes Perikatan ally from muktamar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — PAS has declared that the door to reconciliation with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia within Perikatan Nasional (PN) has closed. PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the breakdown was also why Bersatu had not been invited to the Islamist party’s 72nd muktamar in Pengkalan Chepa, Kelantan, from September 2 to 5. Hadi said PAS had instead invited Umno, as well as other parties in the PN coalition, to attend the muktamar .

items.title: MetMalaysia issues special National Day forecast with thunderstorms, rain and haze expected through the weekend
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Labuan are expected to experience haze throughout the day. In Sabah, thunderstorms and rain are expected to hit the interior and Sandakan throughout the day, while Tawau is expected to experience thunderstorms in the morning and rain at night. The west coast of Sabah, meanwhile, is expected to experience haze throughout the day.

items.title: Muslims must lead by example through morality and integrity, says Anwar
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Aug 29 — Muslims must set the best example for society through good character, integrity, diligence and by rejecting corruption and wrongdoing, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan was also present. The Prime Minister said Muslims must also demonstrate balance in life by prioritising knowledge, faith, morality, spiritual and physical development, as well as material progress.

items.title: Umno invites PAS top leadership to 2026 general assembly, returning muktamar gesture
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Umno will invite PAS’ top leadership to its general assembly next month, reciprocating an invitation extended to Umno leaders to attend the Islamist party’s annual muktamar in Kelantan. Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the move was a gesture of respect towards PAS, Sinar Harian reported today. PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan was previously reported to have invited several senior Umno leaders, including party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, to attend the muktamar .

items.title: Strengthen mental health support in schools: More than just counsellors
items.summary: LETTERS: THE mental health needs of young people are becoming increasingly complex and must be treated as a serious national priority. I therefore believe that schools need a stronger multidisciplinary mental health support system, with greater access to qualified psychologists, in addition to existing school counsellors. There should be a clear referral pathway between schools, psychologists, government health facilities and other appropriate mental health services.

items.title: Fauzi Omar: Sports' fearless pen
items.summary: Datuk Fauzi Omar belongs to this category - a writer whose columns were not merely read, but awaited. He wrote with a sharpness that never felt performative, only purposeful. He called a spade a spade, never softened the blow, never hid behind polite ambiguity, and never insulted the intelligence of his readers.

items.title: Seven Yemeni men investigated over dangerous stunts while celebrating friend's wedding
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Seven Yemeni men, including five public university students, are being investigated after they were seen performing dangerous acts by leaning out of and sitting on the windows of two moving vehicles along Jalan Sungai Besi here. City police Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa confirmed the authenticity of a viral video on Threads showing the group engaging in dangerous acts involving the two vehicles. He said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred about 12.30am yesterday when both vehicles were travelling along Jalan Sungai Besi towards Jalan Bukit Bintang.

items.title: Gang violence, family killings among major crimes this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A suspected turf war between two gangs with alleged links to secret societies is emerging as a possible motive behind a brazen roadside attack in Taman Alam Megah, Shah Alam, which left one man dead and several others injured. Police later said a blue multi-purpose vehicle was also seen crashing into one of the individuals during the incident. As of Wednesday, police had arrested 11 individuals, aged between their 20s and 30s.

items.title: Ecuador ex-president convicted of corruption
items.summary: QUITO: An Ecuadoran court on Friday convicted ex-president Lenin Moreno of accepting bribes from a Chinese company that built the country's biggest hydroelectric dam. The Attorney General's office said that Moreno, who governed from 2017 to 2021, was among four people convicted in the case involving the construction of the Coca Codo Sinclair dam by China's Sinohydro. Moreno remains free pending his sentencing.

items.title: Study proposed to identify pollution sources in Hulu Perak
items.summary: IPOH: The Department of Environment (DOE) is proposing a total maximum daily load (TMDL) study for Hulu Perak to identify and map potential sources contributing to elevated mineral levels in Sungai Rui. Perak DOE senior environmental control officer S. Pravin said the study would provide the state government with technical data needed to make informed decisions and strengthen measures to control pollution at its source. "Since a management board has been established under the Perak government, we have proposed a TMDL study for Hulu Perak.

items.title: Number of missing in deadly Nepal, China floods jumps past 2,400
items.summary: NUWAKOT: The number of people missing in Nepal and China surpassed 2,400 Friday, underscoring the scale of the disaster days after a tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept away villages and killed hundreds. Rescuers were battling through mud even as the threat of new floods loomed, with emergency teams recovering 586 bodies so far – and some of the dead swept downstream as far away as India. The new figures came as Nepal's disaster authority added 933 hydropower workers to a missing persons list already including trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet's sacred Mount Kailash.

items.title: Three ex-PMs, a former minister and landmark rulings: A week in Malaysia's courts
items.summary: The most striking scene came on Thursday, when three former prime ministers - Datuk Seri Najib Razak, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob - were at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex at the same time. Below are some of the major court cases this week: Saravanan charged over RM1.097 million in bribes Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan was charged with three counts of receiving RM1.097 million in bribes linked to the approval of foreign worker quotas. from supporters before making his way into court.

items.title: Norwegians mourn King Harald as son succeeds to throne
items.summary: OSLO: Hugging and laying flowers, thousands of people gathered in Oslo on Friday to pay their respects to Norway's King Harald, who died Friday aged 89 after a reign of three and a half decades. Harald's 53-year-old son immediately succeeded him on the throne as King Haakon VIII. The king is dead.

items.title: JMG: No compromise on Hulu Perak mining violations
items.summary: Its director Nizarulikram Abdul Rahim said the department would continue to take enforcement action against operators found breaching conditions, particularly those involving wastewater, surface run-off and effluent discharge. He said mining activities were subject to strict regulations under the Mineral Development Act 1994, with operators required to ensure wastewater was properly managed and treated before any discharge. "Basically, a mine cannot simply discharge water.

items.title: ‘Merdeka’ from fear and the courage to move forward together — Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz
items.summary: AUGUST 29 — Every Merdeka and Malaysia Day, many in my and the older generation look back with pride at the founders of our nation. Nearly seven decades after Merdeka, and six decades after Malaysia Day, our nation — with her 34-million population — has become an industrialised, trading nation, a major part of global semiconductor supply chains, with millions of professionals. DOSM estimates that Malaysia had almost six million university graduates in 2024.

items.title: A nation was born here: Stadium Merdeka keeps Malaysia’s independence story alive
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Nearly seven decades after witnessing the proclamation of independence, Stadium Merdeka remains a living symbol of Malaysia's freedom, a place that still remembers the day a nation was born. Standing amidst the modern skyline beside the towering Merdeka 118 (Menara Merdeka Maybank), the stadium continues to serve as a vital connection to the nation’s history. Universiti Putra Malaysia’s social anthropology expert Prof Dr Sarjit Singh Gill said Tunku Abdul Rahman’s seven resounding cries of “Merdeka!

items.title: Hizbollah chief again rejects Lebanon-Israel deal, refuses 'surrender'
items.summary: BEIRUT: Hizbollah chief Naim Qassem on Friday again rejected a deal struck between Israel and Lebanon and said his Iran-backed group refused to "surrender" nearly six months after war erupted with Israel. Israel and Lebanon launched US-sponsored direct talks after Hizbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war on March 2 by attacking Israel, which responded with massive strikes and a ground invasion that Lebanese authorities say have killed more than 4,300 people. "The framework agreement is illegitimate, unlawful, humiliating, destructive to Lebanese sovereignty," Qassem said.

items.title: Trump to mark 9/11 at Pentagon, not New York
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday he would mark the 25th anniversary of the Sept 11, 2001, attacks at the Pentagon – but angrily denied skipping a memorial in New York because of a row over a speech. The New York Times reported that Trump originally intended to commemorate the day with remarks at the site of the Twin Towers but changed his plans because the memorial's organisers do not allow speeches. Asked by reporters why he was not going to New York for the anniversary, Trump replied: "Because I'm going to the Pentagon."

items.title: Bird-cage rooms and rooftop dorms expose Malaysia’s migrant housing enforcement gaps
items.summary: Yet, what would normally be considered adequate accommodation for a family of five is home to 15 migrant workers. Some have also resorted to constructing makeshift rooms, where space permits, on the rooftops of shop lots to accommodate foreign workers, particularly those employed in restaurants and supermarkets, and as general workers. Workers from Myanmar, Vietnam and Cambodia interviewed by Bernama said they did not mind living under such conditions.

items.title: Wisma Putra: Two Malaysians found safe after Nepal floods, 55 remain unreachable
items.summary: Foreign Ministry Deputy Secretary-General (Bilateral Affairs) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin said the two Malaysians had been successfully located, but their information and details were still undergoing cross-checking and further verification. Syed Mohamad Hasrin said the figure of 55 was still subject to further verification based on information received from Nepalese authorities and relevant agencies. “The official is assisting in coordinating information, monitoring developments and liaising with the relevant Nepalese authorities,” he said.

items.title: ‘False and baseless’: Teo Nie Ching rejects social media claims linking her to Johor gang activity, lodges police report
items.summary: KULAI, Aug 28 — Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching today denied allegations circulating on social media linking her to gang-related activities in the state and a road accident currently under police investigation. The DAP national vice-chairman said the allegations were false and baseless, stressing that new social media accounts had been created specifically to make accusations against her. “The police, including the Johor police chief, have already held a press conference and announced that 13 suspects had been arrested.

items.title: Stulang assemblyman Andrew Chen returns to lead Johor Opposition after bruising state election
items.summary: KULAI, Aug 28 — Johor Pakatan Harapan (PH) has agreed to appoint Stulang state assemblyman Andrew Chen Kah Eng as Johor’s Leader of the Balancing Force (Ketua Pengimbang). Johor DAP chairman Teo Nie Ching said the appointment had been agreed by all three PH component parties: DAP, PKR and Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah). In the 16th Johor state election held on July 11, Barisan Nasional formed the new state government after winning 48 seats, while PH secured eight.

items.title: Johari Abdul calls for diplomacy to prevent Cambodia-Thailand dispute from straining Asean
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Dialogue and diplomacy must continue to be prioritised in addressing the Cambodia-Thailand border issue to ensure regional peace and stability, said Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul. Johari said the border issue was among the matters discussed during his meeting with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet on the sidelines of the Second Inter-Parliamentary Speakers’ Conference (ISC-2) in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. “Developments along the Cambodia-Thailand border were also among the matters given attention.
